about: The automated review apps whose reviews pr-create, issue-queue, prd-queue, land-prs, code-cleanup, verify-pr and the orchestrator in .dot-agent-deck.toml wait for, read by wait-reviews.sh beside this file (issue #1256). Adding, dropping or replacing a reviewer is an edit here, not in those skills. Each entry says how to tell that the app has finished reviewing a pull request: `comment` is an issue comment by `login` whose body contains `contains`, and with `names_head` it must also contain the head commit's SHA; `check_run` is a completed check-run named `name` on the head, created by the GitHub App whose slug is `app`; `review` is a submitted PR review by `login` whose commit_id is the head. A `comment` without `names_head` marks an app that reviews once, when the PR opens: its `timeout_minutes` counts from the PR's creation. Every other signal marks an app that reviews every push: its `timeout_minutes` counts from when wait-reviews.sh starts, and again whenever the head moves. docs/develop/governance.md, 'The automated reviewer', has the measurements behind each entry.

reviewers.name: Qodo
reviewers.note: Reviews every push and creates no check-run. It edits its one 'Code Review by Qodo' comment in place, and the body ends with <!-- https://github.com/<repo>/commit/<sha> --> naming the commit it reviewed. Over 45 PRs (#1756-#1856) the review landed a median 150 s after the PR opened and at most 1008 s, and its reviews of later pushes at most 869 s after the push, so 20 minutes covers every case seen.

reviewers.name: Greptile
reviewers.note: Reviews once, when the PR opens (greptile.json sets triggerOnUpdates: false), so one summary comment means it is done for the whole PR; a later push gets no review to wait for. The comment is posted when the review completes, seconds before its 'Greptile Review' check-run, which sits on the opening commit rather than the head. Over the same 45 PRs it landed within 463 s of the PR opening, so the 15 minutes count from then. An exhausted monthly quota produces no comment and no check-run, so expect a timeout then.
